proof:
Source and role. This is the difference-quotient estimate for W^{1,p} functions (Evans 5.8.2, Theorem 3(i); Gilbarg-Trudinger 7.11). It controls the mollification error in the sibling w12_ball_rellich_compactness, which is fact (R) of the parent proof. It uses the sibling Submission.w12_ball_smooth_approximation, called (A): for IsW12WithGradient f g B and 0 < s < 1 there are C^infinity functions phi_j with int_{B_s}|phi_j - f|^2 -> 0 and int_{B_s}|grad phi_j - g|^2 -> 0.

Notation as in (A): B_s := ball(0,s), B := B_1. Integrals of nonnegative functions are lintegrals, and ||u||_{2,E} := (int_E |u|^2)^{1/2}.

Proof.
0. Measurability. Assume f and g are strongly measurable by choosing representatives equal to them a.e. on B. For x in B_r, both x and x - z lie in B_{r+|z|}, a subset of B, and translation preserves null sets; so neither side of the claim changes.

1. Smooth estimate. Let phi be in C^1(R^n). For every x, phi(x - z) - phi(x) = - int_0^1 <grad phi(x - tz), z> dt. By Cauchy-Schwarz, |phi(x - z) - phi(x)|^2 <= |z|^2 int_0^1 |grad phi(x - tz)|^2 dt. Integrate over x in B_r and use Tonelli and translation invariance of Lebesgue measure:
int_{B_r} |phi(x - z) - phi(x)|^2 dx <= |z|^2 int_0^1 int_{B_r - tz} |grad phi|^2 dt <= |z|^2 int_{B_{r+|z|}} |grad phi|^2,
because B_r - tz lies in B_{r+|z|} for t in [0,1].

2. Passage to f. Put r' := r + |z|; then 0 < r' < 1. By (A) with radius r', choose C^infinity phi_j with ||phi_j - f||_{2,B_{r'}} -> 0 and ||grad phi_j - g||_{2,B_{r'}} -> 0.
- For x in B_r we have x - z in B_{r'}. So by translation invariance ||phi_j(. - z) - f(. - z)||_{2,B_r} <= ||phi_j - f||_{2,B_{r'}}, and also ||phi_j - f||_{2,B_r} <= ||phi_j - f||_{2,B_{r'}}.
- By Minkowski, u_j(x) := phi_j(x - z) - phi_j(x) converges to u(x) := f(x - z) - f(x) in L^2(B_r), hence int_{B_r} |u_j|^2 -> int_{B_r} |u|^2.
- Also int_{B_{r'}} |grad phi_j|^2 -> int_{B_{r'}} |g|^2, by Minkowski.
Letting j -> infinity in step 1 applied to phi_j gives int_{B_r} |f(x - z) - f(x)|^2 dx <= |z|^2 int_{B_{r'}} |g|^2 <= |z|^2 int_B |g|^2. QED
